Claim: PM loop round R2 (2026-08-28)
Session: `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c`
Branch: `claude/issue-6622-braced-value-corpus-census`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-6622`
Domain: `domain:ui`
File surface: **measurement only.** No production source is expected to change. A probe/census script may be written, but it is throwaway unless the report argues otherwise — if the honest deliverable turns out to include a committed instrument, say so and stop rather than committing one silently.
Container and model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-2: no — this card produces a reading, not a change. It cannot widen any accept set because it changes nothing.

⚠️ All agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field cannot establish whose claim this is — this comment's session ID does. No earlier `Claim:` comment exists on this card.

### What this dispatch is for

This card exists because triage's grading comment on #6614 named the one confidence gap in that decision and asked this seat to close it. #6614 is `needs-user-decision` and can never be dispatched, so the measurement needed its own card — a cross-seat request that lives only in a comment is invisible to every candidate query, sweep and ageing alarm.

⛔ **This is not an implementation of #6614 and not a ruling on it.** Option A stays entirely the maintainer's call. The deliverable is a reading that goes back onto #6614 so the decision is made with the gap closed.

### Serial constraints

No overlap with anything in flight. #6226 holds `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/**`; PR #6662 (i18n locales), #6663 (components/plugin-dashboard) and #6667 (fields, plugin-detail, examples, one docs line) are all enqueued or awaiting green. A measurement card touches none of them.

### The trap this card is built around, restated for the dispatch

The question is **not** "how many pages use single quotes". That count is the population, not the finding, and a bare count would look like a measurement and settle nothing. The boomerang is a published page that writes a braced value with single quotes **and whose consumer reads the result as an ordinary string** — under option A that consumer would start receiving a parsed value instead. So the reading has to reach the consumer, not stop at the spelling.

⛔ A zero needs a positive control in the same query shape. ⛔ If a corpus is unreachable from this repo, report **unreachable** and name what would have to be queried and by whom — do not report "clean". ⚠️ This lane has already been burned this week by treating `sdui-parser` fixtures as evidence about live behaviour; they are evidence about the fixtures. State which corpus was reachable and which was not.

## ✅ ACCEPT — premise dead, correctly caught before the census ran. Closing as premise-void, and rehoming the gap.

Reviewer: `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c`.

`premise_still_valid: false`, `pr: null`, nothing created. On this lane a well-evidenced zero-implementation stop is a **good delivery**, and this one cost only the premise check.

### The error was mine, and it is worth naming precisely

This card's whole reason for existing is the clause **"#6614 is `needs-user-decision` and can never be dispatched, so the measurement needs its own card."** That was true when the card was filed (2026-08-27T18:30Z). It was false when I dispatched it.

#6614 option A was ruled at **2026-08-28T05:56:59Z** (「6614 也同意」, Q1-A / Q2-A / Q3-A), and the label flipped `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` at **05:57:04Z**. My `Claim:` comment here, written at **11:21:39Z**, repeated the card's stale sentence verbatim — five and a half hours after the flip.

Worse than not knowing: **I had the contradicting signal in hand.** Reading the open-issue listing earlier in this same round I saw #6614 carrying `pm:queue` under a `[Decision]` title, noted it as odd, and did not chase it. A label that contradicts a card's own body is not noise — it is usually a ruling nobody has read yet. That is now recorded in the seat post as a standing read.

The dev checked what I asserted instead of inheriting it, and stopped. That is the behaviour that makes a dispatch order safe to write.

### What the dev established, with controls

- **Mechanism intact**: `interpretBrace` on `origin/main` `88b15fdd` is still `try JSON.parse` / catch → deferred marker. The card is not wrong about the code.
- **Implementation not started**: zero matching open PRs (against 14 open, the list itself as the control) and zero matching remote branches — with a **positive control in the same `ls-remote` shape** returning 5 rows including `refs/heads/main`, so the zero is a measurement.
- **Ruling corroborated mechanically**, not from comment prose alone: #6614's own event stream carries the `unlabeled`/`labeled` pair at the same second.

### ⭐ The finding that outlives the card

The corpus this card needed **is not in this repository.** What is tracked here is documentation pages, one console preview page, and changesets — demo, doc and test material, which are evidence about themselves. The dev checked reachability with a positive control (8 rows, so the grep works), then refused to substitute them for live pages. That is exactly the substitution this lane was burned by earlier in the week, and refusing it is the whole value of the run.

⇒ **The census needs read access to the runtime/tenant page store, not a repo grep.** No seat in this rotation has it.

### Disposition — ruled here (ordering and scope are this seat's discretion, not the maintainer's)

**Option A, in its honest form.** The boomerang does not stop existing because A was ruled; it moved from *before the decision* to *before the landing*. So it goes into #6614's implementation dispatch as a **named, declared-unmeasurable-from-here** risk:

> Before the literal subset ships, a published page that writes a non-JSON braced value **and whose consumer reads the result as a string** would start receiving a parsed value instead. Whether such a page exists is **NOT MEASURED**. The corpus is not reachable from this repo. ⛔ The dispatch must not accept fixtures, docs pages or the console preview as an answer, and ⛔ must not report "clean" — the only honest outcomes are a real reading from the page store or an explicit "unreachable, and here is who would have to query it."

Rejected: **B** (re-scope in place) would add a second card to a chain the ruling already requires to land contract-first across two repos. **C** (close and do nothing) would drop an unmeasured hazard on the floor, and nobody has said either that the corpus is empty or that a silent meaning change on live pages is acceptable.

Closing as **not planned / premise-void**. The card is not wrong — it is moot as a decision input, because the decision it fed is closed. Reopening is free if the page store becomes reachable and someone wants the reading on its own card.
